creator: codex
subtasks: S1 execution-lease data plane: owner identity (instance id + started_at) + lease record (thread_id -> owner / acquired_at / heartbeat_at / expires_at / state) + acquire / renew / release / expire_scan. WRITE-ONLY: _background_tasks still decides everything, zero outward behaviour change. New module backend/db/execution_leases.py following the workflow_events in-module fallback precedent.

S2 status derivation reads the lease: has_active_task is answered by the lease instead of the in-process registry; /status and /list orphan semantics change from 'no task in this process' to 'lease expired'. Existing tripwires reshaped by design (not deleted): test_orphan_detection, test_workflow_stale, test_runner_phase_sync, plus the integration files that poke _background_tasks.

S3 automatic takeover of expired leases: startup + periodic scan resuming from the checkpoint. Takeover may resume the execution loop but may NOT make a decision for a human -- side-effecting nodes (publish/login/upload) are never re-run automatically; those park in a human-decision state and emit an event. Same rule as P2a-S4b's default-refuse and P0-W4's unknown reconciliation.

S4 move long tasks out of the orchestration process -- EVIDENCE-GATED (ruling 1): if S1-S3 yield no observable evidence of a long task occupying the API process, this degrades to a document + per-call-site classification (facts 9 and 13). Note fact 9: Chrome already runs on the host, so this is about the CDP client session, not about moving Chrome.

S5 docs/execution-plane.md: what the lease guarantees and does not guarantee, the single-process reality vs the topology docs/deployment.md describes, the no-DB semantics (durability: none), the automatic-takeover safety boundary, and the per-call-site classification.
notes:
PLANNING ROUND (feat/p2b-s1-execution-lease, commit b69883e1) -- reconnaissance and slice plan, no code yet. The ticket was blank (status planning, subtasks [], placeholder jsonl), so this round produced prd.md: fifteen findings each with file:line, a five-slice plan, red lines, acceptance, and the rulings. THE TICKET'S PREMISE WAS REWRITTEN: Dockerfile:81 runs `uvicorn backend.api.app:app --port 8889` with NO --workers, so production is SINGLE-PROCESS (P0's own verification says so at research/p0-claims-verification.md:24) while docs/deployment.md documents a load-balanced three-replica, four-worker topology -- documented end state, not fact. So 'the API process does not hold the real execution lifecycle' is not a defect happening today; what IS happening is that a deploy kills in-flight work and the orphan is only detected, never taken over. Findings that carry the plan: (1) _background_tasks (api/routes/_runner.py:42) documents its own boundary -- cleared on restart, DB rows left at 'running' are 'restart orphans, detected lazily in /list and /status (no startup scan)'; (2) FOUR pieces of process-local state decide what callers observe (_LAST_HISTORY_WRITE, _active_sync_executions, _background_tasks, _last_status at _runner.py:33-45); (3) derive_status(..., has_active_task=True) (state/machine.py:34, priority 9/10 at :129-135) makes RUNNING vs STALE a question about THIS process -- the same checkpoint read elsewhere is a different status; (4) _is_orphan_running (api/routes/workflow.py:389-399) is 'task is None or task.done()', so 'orphan' means 'this process does not have it'; (5) recovery already exists and is human-triggered (POST /recover/{thread_id} at workflow.py:1623, retry_from_last_success via Command(goto=) at :475-491) -- detection exists, automatic takeover does not; (6) there is NO lease/heartbeat/worker/job-queue anywhere in backend/, so the durable scheduler is built from zero; (7) Chrome ALREADY runs out of process on the HOST (docs/deployment.md:284-407), so moving 'XHS Browser' means the CDP client session, not Chrome; (8) db/pool.py is Postgres-only (SQLite is only the dev checkpointer fallback, graph/builder.py:432,612) and the db/ fallback pattern is inconsistent -- workflow_events.py:62-71 has an in-module _mem_events fallback while db/workflows.py has ZERO is_pool_ready checks (the guard is pushed to callers at _runner._db_upsert:71-74). Dependency check: P0's retry consolidation IS delivered (graph/error_handling.py exhaustive RETRY_POLICIES + get_retry_policy raising KeyError), and its comment assigns the 'unified retry engine' to P1/P2 -- recorded as an explicit non-goal. RULINGS (user, 2026-09-16): (1) S4 is evidence-gated -- S1-S3 first, independent worker only if the evidence demands it, else S4 degrades to doc + call-site classification; (2) when is_pool_ready() is false the lease degrades EXPLICITLY with a single reader answering 'durability: none' -- never a silent downgrade, and never fail-closed (that would kill local dev and the whole test suite). Ruling 3 (adopted by discipline, not escalated): automatic takeover may resume the loop but may never re-run a side-effecting node. Tripwires to reshape by design: test_orphan_detection(4), test_workflow_stale(7), test_recover(11), test_publish_retry(8), test_runner_phase_sync(4) plus test_api_routes / test_sse_eventbus / test_workflow_bug_fixes. S1 DELIVERED (feat/p2b-s1-execution-lease, commit 761c2865, PR #614): backend/db/execution_leases.py (+530) is the lease data plane -- owner identity (host:pid:rand + started_at), a per-row ttl_seconds so every expiry judgement reads the row's own budget, and acquire/renew/release/expire_scan/get_lease/list_leases/start_lease/end_lease/ensure_tables/durability, Postgres-first with an in-module fallback following db/workflow_events.py:62-71 (NOT db/workflows.py, which has zero is_pool_ready guards). Wired in at api/routes/_runner.py:327-336 (start, after the sync/async fork, before the try) and :486-492 (end, in the finally after _background_tasks.pop), both inside contextlib.suppress(Exception) because an observational lease must not become a new failure mode; ensure_tables joins the app lifespan's ensure_coros. WRITE-ONLY: nothing reads the lease yet except expire_scan/is_stale, so no answer this service gives changes. cli/main.py is deliberately untouched -- _run_graph_and_persist is only reachable from api/routes/*. Two real defects the tests forced out: acquire judged the incumbent by the CALLER's ttl (which would make one row alive for one reader and dead for another), and the memory fallback handed out the stored object while Postgres builds a fresh record per row. S2 DELIVERED (feat/p2b-s2-status-reads-the-lease, commit b88897d3, PR #615): status derivation reads the lease. _runner gains process_has_active_task (the process registries; verbatim the old inline expression), _lease_is_held (best-effort -- a broken store answers 'not held', not 'held') and has_active_execution (lease OR this process). Seven sites that feed derive_status plus _is_orphan_running moved to it; the two guards that decide whether to START work (brief-upload, publish-retry) deliberately keep reading this process, because both directions are wrong: a bare lease read starts a second execution when the store fails, and asking 'does anyone hold it' refuses a legitimate resume for up to LEASE_TTL_SECONDS after a restart (the dead owner's lease still looks renewable). Orphan semantics change from 'this process has no task' to 'nobody holds the lease'. Fixed an existing defect found on the way: the inline checks at workflow.py:1080 and :1659 had dropped the _active_sync_executions term -- two answers to one question inside one module. Registered cost: inside the 60-90s post-crash TTL window /recover refuses to recover; that is deliberate, bought with red line 4. Reshaped tripwire (not deleted): test_runner_phase_sync::test_phase_falls_back_to_result_when_snapshot_has_no_phase now expects RUNNING -- the old STALE encoded a defect, since only /start's async_mode branch registers in _background_tasks and the foreground /start branch was therefore invisible to has_active_task, which made the runner write 'stale' about a thread it was itself executing.
